children: Artificial intelligence companies are making their mark in the office market, boosting their presence as tenants, especially in San Francisco and New York City, according to a recent analysis by CompStak.

AI's share of new leasing has climbed to 31.3% in San Francisco in the first half of 2026 from 29.7% in 2020. In New York, the growth is even more dramatic, rising to 8.2% of new leasing in H1 2026 from 0.7% in 2020, the real estate data analytics firm said. CompStak partnered with Savills to track how AI firms have matured as office occupiers in the two markets.

AI leasing volume in San Francisco jumped to 2.9M square feet, more than any prior full year and up from 728K square feet in 2020. In New York, AI leasing volume was 1.7M square feet, exceeding the total of 2024 and 2025 combined.

With the increased leasing volume, availability of space is declining in the key submarkets. In Manhattan, office availability in the Park Avenue South submarket dropped to 15.2% from 26.4% in Q4 2023, CompStak said. In San Francisco's Mission Bay/Showplace Square submarket, availability slid to 17.6% from 36.8% in Q4 2023.

Another sign of the AI sector's prominence is that direct leasing is now exceeding its subleasing activity. "Part of the shift is maturation: scaling companies need space that supports long-term occupancy rather than short-term flexibility," the report said.

In H1 2026, subleasing, as a share of AI leasing volume, fell to 23.0% in San Francisco vs. 44.9% in 2020-2024 and 17.9% in Manhattan vs. 42.3% in 2020-2024. Another reason for the lower proportion of subleasing is that the discount to market rates has narrowed.

AI firms aren't just leasing more space; they're leasing for longer. The average AI lease term surged to 90.9 months in Manhattan during the first half of 2026 from 49.0 months in 2020. In San Francisco, the average AI lease term increased to 58.6 months in H1 2026 from 46.3 months in 2020, the report said.
